title: Exalt the Lord Our God
description: Exalt the Lord Our God in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 99, part 2, headed “A holy God worshipped with reverence”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ex-alt the Lord our God, And wor-ship at his feet; His na-ture is all ho-li-ness, And mer-cy is his seat.

lines: When Moses cry'd, when Samuel pray'd,
And oft he made his vengeance known,
Whose grace is still time same;
Still he's a God of holiness,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
